newsitem.title: USA: PartnerRe to buy Swiss Re unit.
newsitem.headline: PartnerRe to buy Swiss Re unit.

text.p: Bermuda-based PartnerRe Ltd said Monday it agreed to buy Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances from Swiss Reinsurance Co. for 5.4 billion French francs, or $950 million, in cash and stock.
Under terms of the definitive agreement, PartnerRe will pay about $800 million in cash and 6.45 million PartnerRe common shares for the Paris-based direct reinsurer, which was founded in 1884.

Swiss Re announced previously that it was acquiring the shares of Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances, also known as SAFR, held by Assurances Generales de France and French insurance group Athena, giving it about 79 percent of the company.
After those transactions, Swiss Re will begin a cash tender offer for the remaining shares held by the public and PartnerRe will then acquire all the shares held by Swiss Re.
PartnerRe said it expected about $550 million of the transaction to be financed by internal resources, with the rest financed by issuing preferred stock or debt.

"At a time when the number of independent providers of reinsurance capacity is decreasing, we believe the combination of PartnerRe and SAFR will create a new choice in global reinsurance," Herbert Haag, president and chief executive of PartnerRe, said in a statement.
PartnerRe said the deal could slightly reduce its operating earnings per share this year, but was expected to add to earnings next year and beyond.

The French company's estimated written premiums for last year totalled $700 million, of which 29 percent originated from France, 44 percent from the rest of Europe, 13 percent from Asia and 14 percent from other countries, including North America, it said.

"SAFR's strong position in Europe and the world's developing markets, combined with PartnerRe's existing strengths, will create global synergies which will translate to added benefit to clients and shareholders through cross-selling opportunities and enhanced utilization of capital," Haag said.
The deal, which was subject to various regulatory approvals, was expected to be completed by mid-year.
PartnerRe's stock lost 62.5 cents to $34.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
